steps: /studio-lab anonymous, Snap off, zoom 40 px/s; stems clip at 2 s (clip root left = ruler x for 2.000 s)
Double-click the stems body at the ruler x for 6.000 s (x = 752 at both viewports)
bugs.expected: E7: the point is added at the pointer's timeline time, the same time the ruler shows at that x (6.000)
bugs.actual: data-envelope = 5.975:1.0000 (status 'Envelope: წერტილი დაემატა — 5.975 წმ · 0.0 dB.'). This happens on every add at both viewports (dt = -0.025 s at 6, 10 and 14). The handler measures x from the clip body, which starts 1 px right of the clip root because of the border. The point is drawn at x = 752, where the ruler reads 6.000, so the drawn point, its label and the audio disagree by 1 px. That is 25 ms at 40 px/s and scales with zoom (100 ms at 10 px/s). A recorded this as the L1 signal. Severity Low (not Medium): the offset is 1 px, smaller than a pointer can place on purpose; it depends on zoom; the point is still placed free, as specified; no data is lost. It does, however, happen on every add.
bugs.evidence: c-round-83/r1-1440x900.json and r1-1280x720.json, row EN-ADD-OFFSET (dt [-0.025,-0.025,-0.025]); EN-DRAWN dx = -1.0 px between the polyline vertex and the point centre; r2-*.json V = 5.975:1.0000;9.975:0.2512;13.975:1.0000

blocked: G83-3 fake-Bearer 403 sub-check: backend unavailable in cloud (/api/studio-token with a fake Bearer token returns 500 'Unable to prepare Studio access', not 403). Not counted as PASS.
signals: EN-LIVE: a narrow ±0.1 s meter window is noisy on the pulse material (control alone ranged -18.6 to -10.6 dB within ±0.1 s). Run 1440-a used that oracle and failed (d10 -5.7, d16 +6.3). Its raw samples were not saved, so its wide-window value cannot be recovered: it counts as one failed measurement. The valid measurements are 1440-b (-11.79 / +0.14 dB) and 1280-a (-11.85 / +0.15 dB), one per viewport. The tolerances (±2 / ±1 dB) were not changed. The windows [9,11] and [15,16.5] come from the plateau geometry (flat between 6.975 and 12.975 and after 13.975), not from the result. The narrow values are kept as EN-LIVE-narrow in r3-*.json.

EN-PLAY-EDIT: one point drag during playback created 6 new buffer sources (window.__src 10 -> 16), because each preview reschedules. Playback stayed monotonic (position advance 2.319 s vs wall clock 2.32 s), with no console error.

X1: with no click count, Chromium produced no dblclick after a fade drag (0 events, as A saw). A dblclick with clickCount=2 sent 24 ms after the drag did reach the handle, and the guard kept the fade. Whether a real human click pair after a 5 px drag makes Chromium emit dblclick was not checked here.

Sticky-header probe (reviewer signal): after scrolling the lane 330 px horizontally in Env mode, the track header (not the z-30 point) is topmost at a point position under the header, at both viewports. The overlap was not reproduced.

At 1280x720 a body range selection shifts the stems lane up 9 px (clip y 458 -> 449, h 71 -> 66). The range code is not part of round 83, so this is probably older behaviour, but it was not checked against bdc2067. It made one C harness step stale; that step was re-run with fresh coordinates.

Setup deviation: in r1 the synthetic video was loaded for EN-MODE and stayed loaded (muted) through EN-ADD … X1, which is why u0 = 'Undo: Mute — ვიდეო'. No oracle depends on it. r2 and r3 ran without video.
